blocks.value: **Using a primitive as a type argument.** `Gen<int>` will not compile. Use `Gen<Integer>`.
**Getting the diamond backwards.** The type on the **left** is required; the right may be `<>`.
**Using a raw type.** `Gen g = new Gen();` compiles with unchecked warnings and abandons every guarantee generics provide.
**Expecting `List<Object>` to accept a `List<String>`.** It will not. Use `List<?>` or `List<? extends Object>`.
**Trying to add to an `extends` wildcard.** `List<? extends Number>` is read-only for its elements: the compiler cannot know which subtype it actually holds. That is PECS enforcing itself.
**Expecting the type parameter to exist at run time.** Generic type information is erased during compilation (*type erasure*), so `new T()` and `T[] arr = new T[10]` are not allowed.
**Naming type parameters like classes.** `Gen<MyType>` reads as a concrete class. Stick to `T`, `E`, `K`, `V`, `N`.
